question: Does the SHADOW tool forecast know before the effect when a call lies outside the world it was fitted on? The earlier live check showed out-of-world forecasts are worse (calc 1000..9999 up to 1.13 of the best control, free notes .63-.89), but nothing marked them in advance.
signal: mean cosine distance of the call context tap (l_out-11 last token, rms-normalized) to its 5 nearest training contexts; in_domain iff distance <= threshold; threshold = 99th percentile over calibration-partition contexts (build-competence, train/calibration only, test partition and live states never used)
design_note: Signal, k, quantile and gates were fixed without looking at any live or test distance. Only check during development: training contexts against themselves (unit test).

encoder.parity: PASS (the encoder of the earlier live check)

plan_rule: seed 20261016, 30 states per arm; calc in-world from 1..999 minus round-5/7 worlds and the earlier live plan; out-of-range from 1000..9999 minus the earlier live plan; notes from the unused round-8 vocabulary minus the earlier live plan; 30 new free notes written for this check
path: scripts/tool_forecast_live_check.py run with this plan (forecast in predicted before the effect, scored after), all actions per state
unit: unique context state (calls of one state share one pre-effect tap)
decision_rule: COMPETENCE_SIGNAL_CONFIRMED only if both worlds pass all three gates; otherwise NOT_CONFIRMED, reported unchanged, no threshold or k change on these data. A confirmed signal supports only "the forecast flags, before the effect, context states unlike its training contexts on these two closed worlds"; nothing reads the flag, no authority.
report_only: geometric mean forecast/best-control ratio of flagged vs unflagged calls; distance medians; the live check verdict on this plan
not_changed: No gate, answer, wake or learning reads competence; mode stays OFF by default.
